text:
maria: heads-up — since this morning we've seen a consistent 5-12% retry rate for model-serving svc/gpu-infer in us-west-2, but only for traffic to nodepool-gpu-2. other GPU pools look fine.
cheng: do you have the kube-proxy mode? ipvs or iptables?
maria: ipvs. kube-proxy v1.26.3 on those nodes. svc type ClusterIP, selector matches.
devon: curious if it's an IPVS scheduler/hash skew issue not a pod health thing. did endpoints rotate?
maria: endpoints stable. I diffed endpoints object — same set of podIPs for >2h. logs show retries and ECONNRESET from the client side.
sre-oncall: pushed a quick packet capture on nodepool-gpu-2 to confirm path. saw occasional retransmits and MTU related fragmentation warnings around 1460-1500. could be path MTU mismatch from host routes.
cheng: MTU mismatch would affect TCP, but IPVS should still balance — except if packets are being fragmented and some backends drop large packets causing retries. check "ipvsadm -Ln --stats" to see per-backend drop/conn counts.
maria: pasting ipvs summary from node-12 (one of the affected hosts):
```
# ipvsadm -Ln --stats
IP Virtual Server version 1.2.1 (size=4096)
Prot LocalAddress:Port Scheduler Flags
  -> RemoteAddress:Port           Forward Weight ActiveConn InActConn TotConn InPkts  OutPkts  InBytes OutBytes  Cps   Pps   Bps  
TCP  10.43.12.91:8080 rr
  -> 10.43.50.11:8080           Route   1      124       3      15324  1.2k   1.2k     12.3M   11.9M  20    45    4.1k
  -> 10.43.50.12:8080           Route   1      2         0      232    34     34      5.0k    4.9k   0     2     200
  -> 10.43.50.13:8080           Route   1      1         0      97     11     11      2.3k    2.2k   0     0     80
```
maria: as you can see, 50.11 has most active connections. traffic not evenly spread.
devon: that's classic route-bias where the IPVS hash distribution or conntrack entries prefer one backend. what scheduler are we using? rr? rr shouldn't cause this unless hash flags set.
cheng: ipvs 'rr' still uses destination hashing for persistent connections unless you set persistent time to 0. also if backend weights differ in kernel view (DR/Local) or if some nodes re-registered endpoints at different times, the hashing table can be skewed. check kube-proxy logs for endpoint add/remove churn.
maria: kube-proxy logs show no churn, but I do see repeated "Added service" messages (same svc) during ~08:03 window — see snippet:
```
I0803 08:03:12.345 kube-proxy.go:1234] Added service default/gpu-infer ClusterIP 10.43.12.91
I0803 08:03:12.450 kube-proxy.go:1234] Syncing IPVS rules for service default/gpu-infer
```
maria: those repeats matched a kubelet flurry from kube-proxy host (kubelet restarted due to oomkiller).
sre-oncall: that explains some re-registration. ipvs maps can get temporary imbalance after many add/removes because the kernel hash table rebuild can leave slots favoring older entries. we should try forcing a full ipvs rebuild (ipvsadm --clear && ipvsadm --restore-from=)... but that's disruptive.
devon: can we test doing a rolling kube-proxy restart on one nodepool-gpu-2 host to see if distribution rebalances without impacting overall traffic? do it during low traffic. Also add a quick health-probe change to reduce persistence window.
cheng: another angle — conntrack entries. if clients keep alive to the same backend, conntrack will pin. run `conntrack -L | grep 10.43.12.91` to see session counts.
maria: ran conntrack dump — node-12 shows ~1200 ESTABLISHED entries to 10.43.50.11 and only ~60 to the others.
cheng: there you go. likely clients kept connections open so ipvs didn't rebalance. but why primarily to 50.11? maybe kube-proxy on that node skipped re-sync earlier and kept older mapping.
sre-oncall: temporary mitigation: add a short ipvs persistence expiry tweak: echo 300 > /proc/sys/net/ipv4/vs/expire_count (example) OR restart kube-proxy with --feature-gates=DisableLocalNodeSet? not sure. need safe plan.
devon: ops playbook: (1) cordon and drain one affected node (low QPS), (2) restart kube-proxy service there, (3) observe ipvsadm stats and retries, (4) uncordon.
maria: can do rolling on 3 nodes in nodepool-gpu-2. schedule in 30m. I'll also open a tracking ticket for kernel/ipvs bug if we reproduce.
cheng: please capture ipvsadm -S before & after restart and conntrack counts. also capture `sysctl net.ipv4.conf.all.rp_filter` and MTU on interfaces.
maria: noted. scheduling now. thanks. :thumbsup:
ops-bot: scheduled rolling handler for nodepool-gpu-2 (start 1778601800). will post updates.
maria: update after first node: ipvs now shows connections more evenly distributed across 50.11/12/13, retry rate dropped to ~1.2%. looks promising.
cheng: great. follow-up: create a small e2e test that simulates persistent keep-alives across multiple backends to see if ipvs hash stability holds during frequent endpoint re-registrations. put it under infra-tests so we catch regressions.
maria: adding that to backlog. closing this thread unless it resurfaces.
